overview: Idarado was a large, interconnected mine-and-mill system spanning the mountains between Red Mountain Valley in Ouray County and the Pandora millsite above Telluride in San Miguel County.
The Idarado Mining Company formed in 1939 by consolidating earlier properties.

timeline.text: The Idarado Mining Company formed in 1939 by consolidating earlier properties.
Wartime development extended the Treasury Tunnel toward the Black Bear vein in 1943–1944, and a 250-ton-per-day mill began treating development ore on the Red Mountain side in 1945.

moreHistory: Wartime development extended the Treasury Tunnel toward the Black Bear vein in 1943–1944, and a 250-ton-per-day mill began treating development ore on the Red Mountain side in 1945.
After Idarado acquired Telluride Mines in 1953, it rebuilt and expanded the Pandora plant; by 1956 ore moved through the connected underground haulage system for processing at Pandora.
The mine produced zinc, lead, copper, silver, and gold and ceased operation in 1978.
Later court-supervised remediation reshaped tailings, drainage, and portions of the industrial landscape, so present ground forms should not be interpreted as unchanged mining-era features.

Component safeguard: treat Red Mountain’s Treasury portal/yard and former millsite, the high-country underground network, and Telluride’s Mill Level and Meldrum portals, Pandora millsite, support buildings, and tailings as linked parts of one parent complex.
